slots.workflow-matrix/title: Fragmented case ownership makes service friction hard to see and govern
slots.workflow-matrix/matrix-takeaway/text: All volumes and baseline observations are synthetic assumptions. Do not present 22% or 14% as validated performance facts or a business case.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-0: The fictional organization handles 18,000 service cases each month.
Cases enter through a portal, a shared operations queue, and three downstream processing systems.
Confirm case volumes, participant boundaries, entry points and current transaction ownership.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-1: Four teams exchange status updates in spreadsheets.
Separate teams maintain status outside the processing record; ownership and escalation need to be traced across the journey.
Map case state, accountable owners, queue handoffs and the evidence retained at each decision.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-2: A synthetic baseline sample suggests 22% of cases need a manual handoff.
Determine which handoffs reflect policy, information gaps, technical failures or duplicated work before choosing automation.
Validate the handoff definition, sampling window and denominator with operations owners.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-3: The sample suggests 14% arrive without enough information for first-pass processing.
Identify missing information at the entry point and record why cases return for clarification or remain in a waiting state.
Validate first-pass completeness and distinguish missing information from genuine new demand.
slots.workflow-matrix/workflow-rows/workflow-4: Discovery must confirm definitions, sample coverage, and ownership before business-case use.
Replacing the portal alone leaves manual exceptions, duplicate case state, and difficult audit reconstruction.
Use validated baseline and journey evidence to define the first release and its acceptance measures.
slots.slide/takeaway: Distributed status ownership creates handoffs and weak audit reconstruction across one service journey.
